name: Generalized Eruptive Keratoacanthoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Generalized Eruptive Keratoacanthoma

criteria.description: Presence of multiple rapidly growing dome-shaped nodules with central keratin-filled craters
Histopathological confirmation showing well-differentiated squamous epithelium with keratin-filled crater
Generalized distribution of lesions involving trunk and extremities
No histological evidence of invasive squamous cell carcinoma
Eruptive onset with spontaneous regression of some lesions over weeks to months

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple rapidly growing keratoacanthoma-like lesions with histopathological confirmation and generalized distribution
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of squamous cell carcinoma and other keratinocytic neoplasms.

laboratory: Possible mild leukocytosis if secondary infection present
imaging: Not routinely required; imaging to exclude invasive malignancy if suspected
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; sporadic cases predominate
other: Histopathology showing well-differentiated squamous epithelium with keratin-filled crater
Immunohistochemistry negative for markers of invasive squamous cell carcinoma

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of fewer but larger lesions
Associated with internal malignancies in some cases

redFlags: Rapid lesion growth with ulceration and bleeding
Failure of lesions to regress spontaneously
Histopathological evidence suggestive of invasive squamous cell carcinoma
references: Wollina U, et al. Generalized eruptive keratoacanthoma: clinical and histopathological features. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2018.
LeBoit PE, et al. Keratoacanthoma and squamous cell carcinoma: a histopathologic perspective. Am J Dermatopathol. 2019.
